page: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server powered by custom 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton processors. Built on the AWS Nitro System, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX.

Performance benchmarks place the m6g.xlarge in the average to weak tiers depending on the workload. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is average at 1489.98, while multi-core performance registers as weak at 5934.04. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for uncached large-block reads and writes at 71.14 GB/sec and 34.79 GB/sec respectively, but weak performance for cached small-block reads at 236.0 GB/sec. General compute benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the weak category.

The instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard CPU execution. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. This hardware profile delivers qualitative cost efficiency by offering dedicated ARM cores and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio for workloads that do not require high-performance x86 vector extensions or local SSD storage.

The m6g.xlarge is suited for general-purpose workloads such as application servers, mid-tier databases, containerized microservices, and caching fleets. Its architectural profile is optimal for multi-threaded applications that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, such as Redis key-value stores, which achieve 4.48 million operations per second, and static web serving, which registers a throughput of 4.91 GB/sec.
